premises.statement: Each worker_id, source_relation, and position_id combination occurs at most once in the enhanced employee base, so omitting that base from the compensation CTE does not change the final join multiplicity.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: comp AS ( SELECT p.position_id,p.source_relation ... FROM staging.stg_workday__position_job_profile p ... ); LEFT JOIN comp ON b.position_id=comp.position_id AND b.source_relation=comp.source_relation
premises.alternative: The contract says compensation/benefits must "Join ebe to position_job_profile" and then join compensation back on "worker_id, source_relation, position_id"; the enhanced employee contract explicitly permits multiple personal or position matches to multiply base rows.
premises.reason: Repeated base records would make the specified compensation construction produce different row multiplicities from this simplified lookup.

premises.statement: The lifecycle model contains at most one matching record per worker_id and source_relation for workers included in the overview.
premises.alternative: Lifecycle has grain "One row per worker_id record from intermediate.int_workday__worker_details", whereas the overview declares "One row per (worker_id, source_relation, position_id, position_start_date)".
premises.reason: Multiple lifecycle records multiply overview rows and can attach different lifecycle metrics to the same employee identifier.

premises.statement: Each worker_id and source_relation has at most one current worker-position-organization relationship.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: WHERE w.effective_end IS NULL ... LEFT JOIN org o ON b.worker_id=o.worker_id AND b.source_relation=o.source_relation
premises.alternative: The contract requires current organization context to apply across the worker's positions but also declares one overview row per "(worker_id, source_relation, position_id, position_start_date)"; no supplied constraint guarantees a single current relationship.
premises.reason: Multiple current relationships, even to the same organization, can duplicate every overview position row.

premises.statement: Every first digit sequence extracted from a compensation_grade_id fits within DuckDB's INTEGER range.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: WHEN try_cast(regexp_extract(compensation_grade_id,'([0-9]+)',1) AS INTEGER)<=15 THEN 'Senior Level' ELSE 'Executive Level'
premises.alternative: The contract requires conversion "to a number" and classifies "missing/non-numeric → 'Ungraded'", without limiting grade numbers to INTEGER.
premises.reason: An overflowing digit sequence becomes NULL during conversion and falls into Executive Level regardless of the intended conversion-failure policy.

fewer.reason: Other transformations follow explicit contract rules, and the position-to-profile uniqueness dependency has already been recorded as c5-1; no fifth distinct unsupported premise was identified.
